newsitem.title: USA: Arafat must reject violence, terrorism - Mordechai.
newsitem.headline: Arafat must reject violence, terrorism - Mordechai.

text.p: Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai on Thursday warned that the fractured Middle East peace process could remain stalled unless Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat rejected violence in and around Israel.

Speaking with reporters before talks with U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen, Mordechai appeared to rule out any temporary halt by Israel of expanding settlements in Jerusalem and the West Bank unless the violence stopped.
"We have to have back our partner, Chairman (Yasser) Arafat," Mordechai said of the Palestinian leader.

"At the beginning, he and his commanders must fight against terrorism and deny all terrorism and all violence in the area. That is necessary for us to take more risk and to move forward with the peace," Mordechai added.

Mordechai, who was scheduled to meet later on Thursday with Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, spoke as the United States pressed to spark new movement in a process stalled by Israeli settlements and by recent bombings and clashes in the Gaza strip and Israeli-occupied West Bank.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is scheduled to meet in Washington next week with President Bill Clinton, who also held talks here this week with Jordan's King Hussein.
